title: DELPHI is now a kernel
subtitle: what that means, in ninety seconds
note: Every {{token}} is filled from the run's own last-run.json by render.mjs. A token with no value stops the render: no number reaches the screen or the narration by hand.

scenes.narration: A kernel is the smallest part of a computer that everything else has to ask permission from. It is kept small on purpose, because a small thing can be checked.
scenes.label: kernel
scenes.sub: the part everything has to ask

scenes.narration: Until this week, DELPHI was a set of scripts that produced biology. The reasons lived in a document beside the result. Documents rot, and the result stays.
scenes.label: the old shape

scenes.narration: Now there is a kernel, and it knows five moves. Evidence. Fact. Law. Verdict. Build. Nothing else is allowed through.
scenes.label: five moves, and no sixth

scenes.narration: Evidence is a quote from a paper, with its page. A fact is one number out of that quote. A law is a theorem, checked by a prover. A verdict is the law applied to the facts.
scenes.label: what each one is
items: evidence — a quote, and where it is printed
fact — one number out of that quote
law — a theorem, checked by Lean
verdict — the law applied to the facts

scenes.narration: The kernel will not hand over a build unless every verdict underneath it holds. When one does not, you get a refusal that names what was missing. The refusing is the feature.
scenes.label: the gate

scenes.narration: It can also answer: cannot assess. Two numbers measured in different bacterial strains are not comparable. A tool that compares them quietly is worse than no tool.
scenes.label: verdicts in this run that refused to guess
scenes.source: measured in different strains and media, so not comparable

scenes.narration: Who needs that. A lab that has to defend a construct it built. A reviewer who wants to see the chain, not the conclusion. A funder asking what a result actually rests on.
scenes.label: who it is for
items: the reviewer who wants the chain
the funder asking what it rests on

scenes.narration: So here is what DELPHI can do now that it could not. Take a logic circuit written in Verilog, the language chip designers use, and compile it into annotated DNA and a protocol a robot can run. Then stop where the published literature runs out.
scenes.label: new, as of today
items: a protocol a robot can run
and a full stop where the papers end

scenes.narration: On the numbers one paper printed for its own logic gates, the worst pair has a noise margin of minus two units. That circuit cannot work, and the kernel says so before anyone clones it.
scenes.label: the worst pair in a published gate set
scenes.source: Stanton et al. 2014, doi:10.1038/nchembio.1411 — the paper's own printed range

scenes.narration: The numbers it could not find came out as draft publications, one per missing measurement. That is the shortest list that would unblock the model, so it is the right thing to send an author.
scenes.label: one per measurement nobody has published
scenes.source: unsigned drafts, placeholder values, not published

scenes.narration: All of it reproduces from one command, and the whole chain is on the page.
scenes.label: every number here traces to a quote
